hits.text:
I can't believe some people are still bearish on $XRP after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sat down with Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse at Ripple Swell 2026!

Brad has described XRP as central to Ripple's vision. 

And now we're seeing the U.S. Treasury Secretary discussing the future of financial technology at Ripple's own conference.

I know the market isn't looking good right now.

 Prices are falling, sentiment is weak, and people are questioning their investments.

But I want you to think about the financial system we're heading into over the coming years.

Because I see a much bigger future for Ripple and XRP than the current market is pricing in.

Let me explain what I've found.

On October 27, Scott Bessent joined Brad Garlinghouse at Ripple Swell 2026.

The discussion focused on America's leadership in digital assets, the international role of the U.S. dollar, and the importance of modern financial infrastructure.

Bessent also connected the future of finance with competition involving artificial intelligence, semiconductors, and digital technology between the United States and China.

Think about the significance of that conversation.

Digital assets are now part of discussions involving America's economic competitiveness and the future of its financial infrastructure.

And Ripple has spent years building technology that serves many of those needs.

Now look at what happened just one day before Bessent appeared at Ripple Swell.

On October 26, Ripple received final OCC approval to establish Ripple National Trust Bank.

This gives Ripple a federally supervised trust-bank structure for specific financial activities, including managing RLUSD reserves, serving as a collateral trustee, and providing fiduciary digital asset custody.

These are important services for financial institutions that need established custody and compliance arrangements before using digital assets.

Imagine an institutional investor wanting to hold tokenized assets, manage digital dollars, and move money internationally.

It needs reliable custody, settlement services, and liquidity.

Ripple is assembling those capabilities within its financial ecosystem.

And the announcements that followed the banking approval made this even more interesting.

On October 27, BNY expanded its collaboration with Ripple.

BNY's Digital Asset Custody platform now supports both XRP and RLUSD.

I want you to pay particular attention to XRP being included.

Institutions now have another established financial provider offering custody infrastructure for the token itself.

BNY also plans to support tokenized investment products issued on XRP Ledger and enable clients to mint and redeem RLUSD directly through its services.

Institutional investors need secure access to digital assets before integrating them into their financial operations.

BNY is helping provide that access.

Now add Robinhood.

On October 27, Ripple announced that Robinhood plans to use RLUSD on XRPL for institutional settlement.

Robinhood is also integrating Ripple Treasury and expanding its relationship with Ripple Prime.

Consider the range of financial services involved.

Institutional settlement, treasury management, digital asset trading, and liquidity services are becoming more connected.

Every new financial platform integrating Ripple's infrastructure expands the opportunities for additional institutional activity.

Then came Coinbase on October 28.

Ripple and Coinbase announced broader RLUSD access through Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange, and the Coinbase retail application.

The supported infrastructure spans XRP Ledger, Base, and Ethereum.

I see an important expansion of digital-dollar distribution taking place.

And there is something else I want you to understand.

The U.S. Treasury's stablecoin strategy connects directly with the financial market Ripple is targeting.

The GENIUS Act became law on July 18, 2025, establishing a federal framework for payment stablecoins.

On August 17, 2026, Treasury issued proposed implementing rules, with January 18, 2027, identified as an expected effective date for relevant licensing restrictions.

Bessent has discussed how dollar-backed stablecoins can increase international access to U.S. dollars and strengthen demand for Treasury securities.

In September 2025, he also discussed a possible tenfold expansion of the roughly $300 billion stablecoin market by the end of the decade.

That represents an illustrative market scenario of approximately $3 trillion.

Think about what a digital-dollar market of that size means for financial infrastructure.

More stablecoin activity means greater demand for custody, transfers, settlement, and currency exchange.

And this brings us to XRP.

RLUSD represents dollar-denominated value. XRP provides native liquidity and cross-currency exchange functionality on XRPL.

Imagine a financial institution holding digital dollars that needs to settle an obligation in another currency.

It needs an efficient conversion route.

XRP Ledger already supports auto-bridging, which routes exchanges through XRP when that offers better pricing than direct conversion.

As more currencies and tokenized assets become available, the commercial opportunity for efficient liquidity routes expands.

This is one of my strongest long-term reasons for holding XRP.

Now consider the institutional assets already moving toward XRP Ledger.

On October 26, Aviva Investors announced a tokenized share class of its Sterling Liquidity Fund on XRPL.

The underlying fund manages approximately £22 billion, following Aviva's earlier tokenized dollar liquidity fund share class launched in July.

That £22 billion represents the fund's total assets, rather than the amount tokenized.

Still, the importance is clear.

An established investment manager is bringing more of its financial products into blockchain-based infrastructure.

Money-market funds are widely used for managing institutional cash and short-term investments.

Tokenizing these products creates more opportunities to connect investment holdings with settlement and collateral services.

On October 27, C2FO announced an initiative with Ripple to bring financing and settlement supporting C2FO Instant Pay onto XRPL using RLUSD.

C2FO's existing early-payment programs have helped businesses access more than $520 billion in working capital over time.

That is C2FO's historical business activity, which shows the scale of the market its XRPL initiative is addressing.

Think about businesses paying suppliers and moving funds through digital settlement systems.

Those transactions involve payments, financing, and sometimes currency conversion.

This is precisely the kind of commercial activity that makes XRP's liquidity functionality interesting.

Brazil is another important development.

On September 29, Ripple and CSD BR announced an initiative using XRPL as an additional recording and auditing layer for securities, beginning with investment fund shares from BTG Pactual.

CSD BR operates infrastructure involving more than BRL 22 trillion in registered assets.

The first phase focuses on recording and auditing, with native issuance and trading representing possible future expansions.

Again, these are established financial institutions working with blockchain-based infrastructure.

Now let's discuss regulation.

On March 17, 2026, the SEC issued an interpretation identifying XRP as an example of a digital commodity, alongside corresponding guidance from the CFTC.

On September 17, the SEC also introduced a temporary innovation exemption concerning certain tokenized U.S. stock trading activities through permissioned blockchain venues.

And during Swell, Bessent discussed coordination between Treasury, the SEC, and CFTC on regulatory clarity following Congress's unsuccessful CLARITY Act effort in September.

These developments matter to institutions assessing compliance, custody, trading, and financial products.

CME also provides regulated XRP futures and options, giving institutional participants established markets for managing XRP exposure.

Now look at Ripple's own business numbers.

On October 28, Ripple reported:

More than 1,700 institutional, corporate, and enterprise relationships.
Over 85 regulatory licenses.
A target annualized product revenue run rate of approximately $900 million by the end of 2026.
More than $16 trillion in transaction value enabled across Ripple's products during 2025.

That $16 trillion represents the broader Ripple business, rather than XRP settlement volume alone.

But these figures show how extensive Ripple's institutional operations have become.

Add the October 14 partnership with DriveWealth, a brokerage infrastructure provider serving more than 100 partners globally.

We're looking at an expanding network of financial businesses accessing payments, custody, treasury services, digital assets, and prime brokerage infrastructure.

And I see major opportunities for XRP across that network.

Here's the part of my analysis that matters most to the token itself.

XRP has several functions on its native ledger.

Every transaction consumes a small XRP fee. The standard fee is 0.00001 XRP, and the base account reserve is 1 XRP.

Those functions support the network.

But the much larger opportunity, in my view, comes from institutional liquidity and cross-currency bridging.

Imagine market makers maintaining XRP inventory to settle transactions between different currencies and tokenized assets.

As more financial institutions begin using XRP-based exchange routes, those liquidity requirements become an important part of XRP's economic role.

That's the development I want to see reflected in actual settlement volumes, institutional XRP holdings, and deeper trading liquidity.

Now think about the next several years.

Late 2026 is bringing major custody, regulatory, and institutional infrastructure developments.

During 2027, stablecoin regulation and broader institutional settlement adoption become especially important.

From 2027 through 2028, tokenized funds, trade finance, and financial-market infrastructure present further opportunities for XRPL.

Toward 2030, my bullish thesis centers on XRP becoming an increasingly important liquidity asset connecting different financial markets.

I see Ripple building toward a future where institutional digital finance becomes a normal part of global banking.

And I want XRP positioned at the center of that transformation.

Scott Bessent's appearance at Ripple Swell was a discussion about U.S. financial policy, rather than a government endorsement of XRP.

The reason I'm so bullish is the combination of that policy direction with Ripple's expanding institutional infrastructure.

The banking approval, BNY custody, Robinhood, Coinbase, Aviva Investors, C2FO, CSD BR, and the regulatory developments all fit into a much larger financial transition.

The market is focused on today's price. I'm focused on what Ripple and XRP are building for the next decade.

I've been bullish on XRP's long-term financial utility for years, and these developments strengthen that conviction.

Think in years, guys. 

The transformation of global financial infrastructure is much bigger than a few difficult months in crypto.
